source: Salesforce Apex heap and CPU limit observations at API 62.0, 67.0 and 68.0, identical at each version. HEAP-S runs anonymously and HEAP-ST is the same expression in a test method. HEAP-Q, HEAP-F, HEAP-B and HEAP-SCH read the limits inside a Queueable, an @future method, a Batchable execute and a Schedulable execute run by Test.stopTest. The HEAP-SA/SR twins grow a list of distinct 100,001-character strings to about 8 MB and 12 MB, synchronously on both routes (the E rows end normally); HEAP-QA/QR grow a Queueable to about 20 MB and 30 MB. None of those throws a LimitException. MatchFields rows compare the listed fields of the observation; heap byte counts are the platform's own accounting and are not compared. Native anonymous rows report success or the uncaught exception; test rows report each test failure or pass. The HEAP3 rows, at API 62.0 and 67.0, grow further: a String list is accepted at about 15, 20 and 30 MB synchronously and 40 MB in a Queueable, and throws 'Apex heap size too large: <heap>' on the allocation that first passes about 50 MiB (sync at 60 MB, both routes and ending normally or not; Queueable at 60 and 100 MB). Those throw rows assert in strict mode, since permissive mode never throws a LimitException, and compare the message without its byte count. One large String of 15,000,000 or more characters throws 'String is too long.' instead; those rows are asserted in both modes. Dedicated String allocation observations pin a 10,000,000 UTF-16-unit maximum for repeat without a separator, a catchable StringException for concatenation above that length, and a separator-repeat success at 10,000,001 units. The HEAP4 rows, at API 62.0 and 67.0 on the test route, show Scheduled, Batch and @future execute share that threshold: each accepts about 40 MB and throws on the allocation that first passes about 50 MiB.
